test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 12 Sept 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: What is the term of Panchayat Body in India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**5 years**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The term of a Panchayat body in India is** five years **from the date of its first meeting after being elected.
 
• This applies to all levels of the Panchayati Raj system: **Gram Panchayat (village level), Panchayat Samiti (block level), and Zila Parishad (district level).**
 
• **If a Panchayat is dissolved** before the completion of its term, fresh elections must be conducted.
 
• And the newly elected body will serve the **remainder of the five-year term.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **73rd Constitutional Amendment Act (1992)** gave constitutional status to the Panchayati Raj institutions (PRIs).
 
• It added **Part IX** titled "The Panchayats" and introduced Articles 243 to 243-O in the Indian Constitution.
 
• **Article 243A:** Provides for the Gram Sabha, which consists of all adult members registered in the electoral rolls of a village.
 
• **Article 243B:** Provides for the establishment of a three-tier system of Panchayati Raj in every state.
 
• **Article 243C:** Deals with the composition of Panchayats at various levels, based on direct elections from the respective constituencies.
 
• **Article 243D: **Provides for the reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes (SCs), Scheduled Tribes (STs), and women (not less than one-third of the seats).
 
• **Article 243E** Specifies the duration of Panchayat bodies (5 years), and provisions for fresh elections before the end of the term or in case of dissolution.
 
• **Article 243G:** Empowers Panchayats with authority to function as institutions of self-government, and to plan and implement schemes for economic development and social justice.
 
• **Article 243H**: Grants powers to Panchayats to impose taxes, duties, tolls, and fees, and to receive funds from various sources such as state governments.
